title: Dino Park: Ridgeback Rangers
shortDescription: Dino park manager: send rangers, feed herds, hatch eggs, keep the island calm.
fullDescription:
The gate opens at eight. The triceratops are staring at an empty feeder, two kentrosaurus are squaring up over a patch of ferns, a rain squall is rolling in over the hills and the safari tram is already full. You are the new Chief Warden of Ridgeback Isle. Keep the island calm.

Ridgeback Rangers is a dino park management game about running the day, not tapping for coins. Plan the morning, send the right rangers to the right problems, decide which animals share a paddock and keep the visitors moving.

RUN THE PARK DAY
- Set the feed board each morning: how many crates go to each feeding station. Too few and a herd goes hungry, too many and they spoil in the heat.
- Plan the tram timetable. A longer loop needs more cars, or visitors give up and walk.
- Open the park and watch visitors stream in, ride the safari tram and stop at the viewpoints.
- Read the day report: visitors, tram riders, animal care, profit and your Sanctuary Rating.

DISPATCH YOUR RANGERS
- Problems pop up as pins on the living island: a hungry herd, a squabble, a sick animal, a loose fence tile, an animal wandering onto a path, a flooded path.
- Four ranger roles: Feeder, Vet, Handler and Fence Tech. Every pin needs the right one.
- Rangers head out along the service road and take real time to get there. Teams are scarce, so you decide what comes first.
- Unlock the Chief Ranger to answer routine pins for you, or keep every call in your own hands.

HANDLE THE CHAOS
Heat waves, rain squalls, dust storms, a late supply boat and a sudden rush of school groups keep every day different. Nobody on Ridgeback Isle ever gets hurt: a missed pin costs coins and calm, never animals or progress.

PAIR THE HERDS
- Every species has a diet, a home biome and a temperament: calm, skittish or bossy.
- The harmony card shows which animals can live together. Good pairings mean fewer squabbles.
- Visitors love variety: a mixed paddock beats six of the same animal.

DIG, HATCH, GROW
- Send dig crews to fossil sites. Every site shows exactly which species it can yield. No random boxes.
- Move eggs to the incubator, keep the temperature in the warm band and watch them hatch.
- Grow from Landing Cove to the forests of Fern Valley and the hot dunes of Dune Mesa, with eight species including Triceratops, Kentrosaurus, Parasaurolophus and Camarasaurus.
- Build paddocks, stronger fences, water points and shade sails, open a cafe and a gift shop, hire rangers and add tram cars.
- While you are away the sanctuary keeps taking donations, and a welcome-back card shows what came in.

A LIVING ISLAND
Herds roam, the tram loops past the paddocks, rangers cross the island and storms roll over a warm, hand-built diorama. A step-by-step guide shows every action the first time, and you can replay it from Settings. Choose Low, Medium or High graphics to suit your phone, and play at 1× or 2× speed.

GOOD TO KNOW
- Single-player. No account and no sign-in. Your sanctuary is saved on your device.
- The game contains ads and optional in-app purchases: one-time upgrades, tram looks and coin packs. Nothing is needed to finish the game.
- Ads show our other games in a banner and between days. Remove Ads, the Chief Warden Edition, the Ranger Pass and the Complete Sanctuary Collection remove them. Other purchases do not remove ads.
- Reward videos are always optional. With ad removal you get the same capped rewards without a video.
- Coin packs are used up and are not restored on a new device.
- Ten languages: English, Turkish, German, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Russian, Japanese, Korean and Hindi.

If you like dino park games, zoo management and safari park tycoons, pin on the Chief Warden's badge and keep Ridgeback Isle calm.
